delegate.routingGuidance: Luna routes are for bounded background work, Terra routes trade higher cost for lower latency when the parent is blocked, and Sol routes are for maintainer judgement rather than harder implementation. Escalate thinking only within a matching task shape.

luna-low.useFor: Bounded background work that is fully mechanical with one deterministic answer: a named-file lookup, exact rename, generated fixture, or command-and-report task with an exact verifier.
luna-low.avoid: Discovery, judgement, or any task whose finish line is not already decided.

luna-medium.useFor: Bounded background work with a failing test or exact specification: check one named invariant, confirm a fix, or implement a localized change inside one subsystem and a few files.
luna-medium.avoid: Open-ended review, cross-subsystem work, security reasoning, or choosing the design and finish line.

luna-high.useFor: Default bounded background implementation or review where the architecture, scope, acceptance criteria, and relevant files are known; established-pattern multi-file work fits here.
luna-high.avoid: A short wall-clock deadline, open-ended judgement, broad high-stakes review, or work likely to require sustained exploration across subsystems.

luna-xhigh.useFor: Difficult bounded background implementation, diagnosis, regression review, or security verification spanning multiple files or subsystems, with explicit acceptance criteria or named security invariants.
luna-xhigh.avoid: Foreground work blocking the parent on a deadline, unclear criteria that require maintainer judgement, or unbounded repository-wide review.

terra-medium.useFor: Interactive bounded multi-file work where lower latency justifies higher cost, especially when a foreground delegate blocks the parent.
terra-medium.avoid: Background or parallel work without urgency, mechanical tasks, quality-first work with no deadline, or broad difficult analysis.

luna-max.useFor: Difficult bounded background work expected to need unusually deep exploration or verification; select it directly when that depth is predictable.
luna-max.avoid: Short deadlines, interactive foreground work, tasks without a bounded finish line, or assuming more reasoning replaces Sol-style judgement.

terra-high.useFor: Interactive hard repository work with explicit criteria when lower latency justifies higher cost and the parent is blocked on the result.
terra-high.avoid: Background work without urgency, rote edits, open-ended maintainer judgement, or choosing it merely because Luna high was insufficient.

sol-medium.useFor: Judgement about the work rather than a generic strength escalation: decide whether a diff overclaims, whether complexity is earned, what completion should mean when criteria are unclear, or assess ambiguous or high-stakes security concerns. Strict maintainer-style review.
sol-medium.avoid: Mechanical correctness sweeps, implementation against explicit acceptance criteria, or any task adequately served by a Luna background route or Terra latency route.

terra-xhigh.useFor: Difficult interactive work with explicit criteria when the parent needs the deepest latency-oriented route and the higher cost is justified.
terra-xhigh.avoid: Generic background quality escalation, claiming a proven React specialization, broad security or race review without a local evaluation, or work where Luna max latency is acceptable.

sol-high.useFor: Cross-stage integration review spanning several commits where a missed defect is expensive and the failure could be anywhere. Reserve for when Sol medium has already looked and its result was not enough.
sol-high.avoid: Generic hard implementation, deadline routing, or any task with an explicit pass/fail criterion that a cheaper branch can verify.
